#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Toy loop: the 5 pieces with no model at all. The "agent" is one line of shell.
set -u
OBJETIVO=5                         # 1. goal: saida.txt with 5 lines
ESTADO=estado.txt                  # 2. state: lives in a file, not in memory
MAX_CICLOS=8                       # 5. stop: cap on cycles
touch saida.txt
ciclo=$(cat "$ESTADO" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
while true; do
  feitas=$(wc -l < saida.txt)      # 4. check: one command, before acting
  echo "ciclo $ciclo: $feitas de $OBJETIVO linhas"
  if [ "$feitas" -ge "$OBJETIVO" ]; then echo "PRONTO no ciclo $ciclo"; exit 0; fi
  if [ "$ciclo" -ge "$MAX_CICLOS" ]; then echo "PARADO: teto de $MAX_CICLOS ciclos"; exit 2; fi
  ciclo=$((ciclo + 1)); echo "$ciclo" > "$ESTADO"
  echo "item $ciclo" >> saida.txt  # 3. action
done

Quanto mais longa a sessão, mais cheia a: The longer the session, the fuller the context window. The harness compacts: it keeps the goal and shrinks the old steps. Compacting too much loses detail; that's why long loops keep state in a file (lesson 5) and course 2 covers the context bands.

O modelo só produz texto. Quando esse te: The model only produces text. When that text is a tool request (read a file, run a command, edit), the harness executes it and hands the result back to the model. MCP is the standard way to plug in tools from other systems.
Sem verificação o modelo olha o código e: Without verification, the model looks at the code and says "looks good." With it, the model runs the test and reads the result. A real result is worth more than the AI saying it's fine. This is the piece the loop needs most (lessons 1 and 6; course 1).
o que pode, o que pergunta: what it can do, what it asks about
O harness confere cada ação antes de exe: The harness checks each action before running it: editing goes through, deleting asks. Hooks run your scripts before and after tools; the sandbox limits what a command can reach. In a loop with nobody watching, this is what holds back the blast radius (course 4).
o modelo decide o próximo passo: the model decides the next step
o resultado volta para ele: the result goes back to it

O processo ganha uma versão atual, um ro: The process gets a current version, a short script followed in every run, so that two runs can be compared. The Executor produces the artifact and logs one line. It doesn't opine, doesn't suggest, doesn't change its own prompt.
Uma linha por execução, sempre as mesmas: One line per run, always the same columns, result as yes or no. The Observer turns the lines into evidence: counts by version and variant, no adjectives. If the data doesn't match the schema, it stops the cycle.
O Crítico diz o que funcionou e o que fa: The Critic says what worked and what failed, with the strength of the evidence, without proposing a fix. The Optimizer writes hypotheses in the format SE, ENTÃO, PORQUE and MUDANÇA, without repeating discarded ones. The Guardian vetoes anything that touches what never changes or the cap; the veto is final and it doesn't negotiate.
O Experimentador desenha o teste A contr: The Experimenter designs the A versus B test, with the minimum sample calculated beforehand. The Evaluator answers one of three: B_GANHOU, A_SEGUE or AMOSTRA_INSUFICIENTE. There is no "it's winning". The Memory records everything without erasing, and the Meta-agent looks at the system (cost, vetoes) and only reports.
Promovida ou descartada, a decisão vai p: Promoted or discarded, the decision goes to memory and the next cycle starts from the new evidence.
